questions.q: What exercise does Prose recommend for understanding word choices?
a: Imagining synonyms the author could have used
Counting how often each word appears
Reading the author's biography first
Reciting the passage aloud from memory
questions.why: Lesson 1 suggests swapping in synonyms to see why the writer picked the word they did.

questions.q: Why does the summary treat paragraphs as the most personal element?
a: Their first and last words show what the author values
They stay the same length across every book
They reveal how the author edited the text
They mark the places where the plot changes
questions.why: Lesson 2 says a paragraph's emphasis falls on its opening and closing words.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest you read a paragraph?
a: Breathe in at the start and exhale as you finish
Pause only at the last sentence of a page
Skim it once and return to it later
Read it backwards to catch mistakes
questions.why: Lesson 2 compares paragraphs to breathing guides, with a full exhale on the final word.

questions.q: What three things reveal a character's intentions?
a: Actions, thoughts and dialogue
Setting, weather and timing
Names, titles and family history
Chapter titles and footnotes
questions.why: Lesson 3 says what characters think, say and do brings them to life.

questions.q: Which book does the summary use as an example built almost entirely on dialogue?
a: The Little Prince
Harry Potter
The Alchemist
Moby Dick
questions.why: Lesson 3 says The Little Prince runs on conversation, while Harry Potter leans on inner thought.
